overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how machine learning systems and language models work. You'll be asked about rules and learned patterns, kinds of learning, generalization and overfitting, neural networks and their parameters, loss and gradient descent, tokens and embeddings, and next-token prediction.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: A tax program built from written rules handles every return correctly until someone enters a kind of income its programmers never planned for. The program then stops with an error. Which term names this behavior?

options.html: Overfitting, since it fit its examples too closely
options.text: Overfitting, since it fit its examples too closely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: Brittleness, since it fails outside its rules
options.text: Brittleness, since it fails outside its rules
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Brittleness is the tendency of a system to work inside the boundary of its rules and fail abruptly outside it.

options.html: Randomness, since its results vary by chance
options.text: Randomness, since its results vary by chance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: Generalization, since it handles unfamiliar cases
options.text: Generalization, since it handles unfamiliar cases
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

forms.stemHtml: A team trains a model on emails that staff have each marked "spam" or "not spam." Which kind of learning is this?

options.html: Unsupervised learning, since the model finds its own groups
options.text: Unsupervised learning, since the model finds its own groups
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Self-supervised learning, since the emails supply the answers
options.text: Self-supervised learning, since the emails supply the answers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Supervised learning, since people labeled each example
options.text: Supervised learning, since people labeled each example
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In supervised learning every training example comes with the correct answer attached, and here people supplied those labels.

options.html: Rule-based learning, since staff wrote the spam criteria
options.text: Rule-based learning, since staff wrote the spam criteria
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

forms.stemHtml: A model scores very well on its training data and much worse on examples that were held back and never shown to it. What is the most likely explanation?

options.html: The model generalized well from its training examples
options.text: The model generalized well from its training examples
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: The model was given too few parameters to adjust
options.text: The model was given too few parameters to adjust
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: The model's held-back examples were labeled by hand afterward
options.text: The model's held-back examples were labeled by hand afterward
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: The model overfitted to quirks of its training examples
options.text: The model overfitted to quirks of its training examples
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A large gap between the training score and the score on held-back examples is the standard sign of overfitting.

forms.stemHtml: One of the numbers coming into an artificial neuron has a weight near zero. What effect does that number have on the neuron's result?

options.html: It counts for almost nothing in the result
options.text: It counts for almost nothing in the result
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A weight sets how much an incoming number counts toward the neuron's result. With a weight near zero, the number is almost ignored.

options.html: It counts against the other incoming numbers
options.text: It counts against the other incoming numbers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: It counts for more than any other number
options.text: It counts for more than any other number
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: It stops the neuron from passing a number on
options.text: It stops the neuron from passing a number on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these statements about a neural network's parameters are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: They start at random values before training
options.text: They start at random values before training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is random initialization. Training then adjusts the values.

options.html: Their values are set by training
options.text: Their values are set by training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Parameters are the adjustable numbers in a model, and training sets them.

options.html: Each one stores a single fact the model knows
options.text: Each one stores a single fact the model knows
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

options.html: Engineers type in each final value by hand
options.text: Engineers type in each final value by hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

forms.stemHtml: What is the loss in training?

options.html: The share of the training data a model was unable to keep
options.text: The share of the training data a model was unable to keep
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: A single score for how wrong a model's predictions are
options.text: A single score for how wrong a model's predictions are
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The loss combines prediction errors over many examples into one number that training works to bring down.

options.html: The number of parameters removed from a model in training
options.text: The number of parameters removed from a model in training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: The time a model takes to give a prediction for one input
options.text: The time a model takes to give a prediction for one input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

forms.stemHtml: Which description fits gradient descent?

options.html: Trying every possible setting and keeping the best one found
options.text: Trying every possible setting and keeping the best one found
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: Setting each parameter by hand after reading the examples
options.text: Setting each parameter by hand after reading the examples
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: Nudging each parameter slightly in the way that lowers loss
options.text: Nudging each parameter slightly in the way that lowers loss
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Gradient descent repeatedly works out which way to nudge each parameter to lower the loss, then nudges each one slightly.

options.html: Storing each example and comparing new inputs against them
options.text: Storing each example and comparing new inputs against them
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

forms.stemHtml: Tokenization turns the common word "house" into one token and the rarer word "unhelpfully" into three. What accounts for the difference?

options.html: Rarer words are split into several pieces
options.text: Rarer words are split into several pieces
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Common words usually get a token of their own. Rarer words are split into several subword tokens from the model's fixed vocabulary.

options.html: Longer words are always split letter by letter
options.text: Longer words are always split letter by letter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: Rarer words are missing from the training text
options.text: Rarer words are missing from the training text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: Longer words are stored in a second vocabulary
options.text: Longer words are stored in a second vocabulary
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these statements about embeddings are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Tokens used in similar ways end up near each other
options.text: Tokens used in similar ways end up near each other
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Similar use gives similar positions, which is how a model represents similarity in meaning.

options.html: People assign each token its position by hand
options.text: People assign each token its position by hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

options.html: The positions are learned during training
options.text: The positions are learned during training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Embeddings are parameters. They start random and training sets their values.

options.html: Words with similar spelling are placed together
options.text: Words with similar spelling are placed together
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

forms.stemHtml: How does a language model produce a reply that is several sentences long?

options.html: It writes a full draft, checks it, and then releases it
options.text: It writes a full draft, checks it, and then releases it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: It finds the closest stored answer and copies it out
options.text: It finds the closest stored answer and copies it out
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: It picks all of the words at once and then orders them
options.text: It picks all of the words at once and then orders them
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: It adds one token at a time, based on the text so far
options.text: It adds one token at a time, based on the text so far
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is autoregressive generation. Each chosen token is added to the text before the next prediction is made.

forms.stemHtml: A help-desk program answers by matching each message against a list of if-then rules. It gives an error when a customer phrases a request in a way no rule covers. What does this show about rule-based systems?

options.html: They fit the quirks of their training examples too closely
options.text: They fit the quirks of their training examples too closely
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: They gradually lose accuracy as inputs become less familiar
options.text: They gradually lose accuracy as inputs become less familiar
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: They need labeled examples before they can handle a request
options.text: They need labeled examples before they can handle a request
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: They fail abruptly on cases their authors didn't anticipate
options.text: They fail abruptly on cases their authors didn't anticipate
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is brittleness. A rule-based system works inside the boundary of its rules and fails abruptly outside it.

forms.stemHtml: A retailer gives a system its customers' purchase records, with no labels, and asks it to find groups of customers who buy similar things. Which kind of learning is this?

options.html: Unsupervised learning, since there are no labels at all
options.text: Unsupervised learning, since there are no labels at all
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In unsupervised learning the examples have no labels and the system looks for structure in the data on its own.

options.html: Supervised learning, since the retailer supplies the records
options.text: Supervised learning, since the retailer supplies the records
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Self-supervised learning, since part of each record is hidden
options.text: Self-supervised learning, since part of each record is hidden
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Rule-based learning, since the groups are fixed in advance
options.text: Rule-based learning, since the groups are fixed in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

forms.stemHtml: A model is trained to tell wolves from dogs. Every wolf photograph in its training data has snow in the background. The model labels a dog standing in snow as a wolf. What went wrong?

options.html: The model memorized every photograph and looked this one up
options.text: The model memorized every photograph and looked this one up
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: The model learned a shortcut that fit its training examples
options.text: The model learned a shortcut that fit its training examples
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model fit a quirk of its examples, snow, in place of the pattern that separates wolves from dogs. That's overfitting.

options.html: The model was trained with unsupervised learning by mistake
options.text: The model was trained with unsupervised learning by mistake
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: The model followed a written rule about snowy backgrounds
options.text: The model followed a written rule about snowy backgrounds
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

forms.stemHtml: An artificial neuron receives two numbers. The first has a large weight and the second has a negative weight. How do the two numbers affect the neuron's result?

options.html: The first is nearly ignored, and the second counts for a lot
options.text: The first is nearly ignored, and the second counts for a lot
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: The first counts against, and the second is nearly ignored
options.text: The first counts against, and the second is nearly ignored
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: The first counts for a lot, and the second counts against
options.text: The first counts for a lot, and the second counts against
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A weight sets how much an incoming number counts. A large weight makes it count for a lot, and a negative weight makes it count against.

options.html: The first is passed on unchanged, and the second is removed
options.text: The first is passed on unchanged, and the second is removed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

forms.stemHtml: A company wants to correct one wrong fact in a trained model by editing its parameters directly. Which of these are reasons this is hard? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The fact is spread across many parameters
options.text: The fact is spread across many parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! What a network learned is a distributed representation, and no single parameter holds a fact.

options.html: The parameters are deleted once training ends
options.text: The parameters are deleted once training ends
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

options.html: Each parameter also takes part in other outputs
options.text: Each parameter also takes part in other outputs
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Changing the parameters involved in one fact changes everything else they take part in.

options.html: The parameters are sentences that must be rewritten
options.text: The parameters are sentences that must be rewritten
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

forms.stemHtml: A video service trains its recommendation model with an objective that scores how long people keep watching. What will the model become good at?

options.html: Recommending videos that are accurate and well sourced
options.text: Recommending videos that are accurate and well sourced
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: Recommending videos that viewers later say they valued
options.text: Recommending videos that viewers later say they valued
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: Recommending videos from the widest range of creators
options.text: Recommending videos from the widest range of creators
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: Recommending videos that hold people's attention
options.text: Recommending videos that hold people's attention
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model gets good at what the objective scores. Nothing in this score rewards accuracy or later satisfaction.

forms.stemHtml: Gradient descent is often pictured as a walker on a hillside in thick fog who wants to reach the valley. Which action by the walker matches the method?

options.html: Surveying the whole hillside and walking straight to the lowest point
options.text: Surveying the whole hillside and walking straight to the lowest point
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: Feeling the slope and taking a short step downhill, again and again
options.text: Feeling the slope and taking a short step downhill, again and again
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Height stands for the loss and position for the parameter settings. Gradient descent works out which way lowers the loss, adjusts each parameter slightly, and repeats.

options.html: Standing still and waiting for someone to describe the way down
options.text: Standing still and waiting for someone to describe the way down
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: Jumping to random spots and keeping whichever one is lowest so far
options.text: Jumping to random spots and keeping whichever one is lowest so far
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

forms.stemHtml: A user types an unusual surname that the model has never met. How does tokenization deal with it?

options.html: It replaces the surname with a blank the model ignores
options.text: It replaces the surname with a blank the model ignores
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: It adds the surname to the vocabulary as a new entry
options.text: It adds the surname to the vocabulary as a new entry
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: It splits the surname into smaller pieces it has
options.text: It splits the surname into smaller pieces it has
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Rare and unfamiliar words are split into several subword tokens from the model's fixed vocabulary.

options.html: It swaps the surname for the nearest common word
options.text: It swaps the surname for the nearest common word
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers found that starting at the position of "king" and moving in the direction from "man" to "woman" arrives near "queen." Which conclusions does this support? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A direction in the space can stand for a relationship
options.text: A direction in the space can stand for a relationship
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The same step links other pairs of words that are related in the same way.

options.html: Word positions encode more than similarity alone
options.text: Word positions encode more than similarity alone
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The finding showed that relationships between words are captured as well as nearness.

options.html: Someone programmed the royal titles into the model
options.text: Someone programmed the royal titles into the model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

options.html: The model looks up each word in a stored dictionary
options.text: The model looks up each word in a stored dictionary
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

forms.stemHtml: Two runs of the same prompt match for three words and differ at the fourth. From there on, the two replies go separate ways. Why does one different word change everything after it?

options.html: The model restarts with new parameters after any change
options.text: The model restarts with new parameters after any change
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: The model switches to a different vocabulary for each run
options.text: The model switches to a different vocabulary for each run
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: The model predicts each token from the text so far
options.text: The model predicts each token from the text so far
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A reply is produced one token at a time, and each chosen token is added to the text before the next prediction is made. A different word changes the input for every later prediction.

options.html: The model drafts each reply in full before showing it
options.text: The model drafts each reply in full before showing it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

forms.stemHtml: An expert system for medical diagnosis is given a patient whose condition falls outside every rule its authors wrote. What should you expect from it?

options.html: An error or a wrong answer
options.text: An error or a wrong answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A rule-based system doesn't make a reasonable guess when its rules don't cover an input. It works inside the boundary of its rules and fails abruptly outside it.

options.html: A reasonable guess based on similar patients
options.text: A reasonable guess based on similar patients
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: A new rule written to cover the condition
options.text: A new rule written to cover the condition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

options.html: A request for labeled examples of the condition
options.text: A request for labeled examples of the condition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on rule-based programs.

forms.stemHtml: A model is trained on ordinary text by hiding the next word at each point and having the model predict it. Which kind of learning is this?

options.html: Supervised learning, since people mark the correct words
options.text: Supervised learning, since people mark the correct words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Self-supervised learning, since the text supplies the answers
options.text: Self-supervised learning, since the text supplies the answers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The hidden word is the label, so the data provides its own answers and no human labeling is needed.

options.html: Unsupervised learning, since no correct answers are involved at all
options.text: Unsupervised learning, since no correct answers are involved at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

options.html: Rule-based learning, since grammar rules decide each word
options.text: Rule-based learning, since grammar rules decide each word
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised learning.

forms.stemHtml: Why do builders set some examples aside before training and never show them to the model?

options.html: To reduce the amount of data the model has to store
options.text: To reduce the amount of data the model has to store
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: To give the model extra examples if training goes badly
options.text: To give the model extra examples if training goes badly
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

options.html: To check how the model does on inputs it hasn't seen
options.text: To check how the model does on inputs it hasn't seen
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Held-back test data shows whether the model generalizes. A good training score alone doesn't show that.

options.html: To remove the examples that were labeled incorrectly
options.text: To remove the examples that were labeled incorrectly
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on generalization and overfitting.

forms.stemHtml: In a neural network, what does a weight do?

options.html: It records how many examples the network has been trained on
options.text: It records how many examples the network has been trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: It sets how many neurons there are in each of the layers
options.text: It sets how many neurons there are in each of the layers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: It marks which neuron holds a particular fact or concept
options.text: It marks which neuron holds a particular fact or concept
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on artificial neurons, weights, and layers.

options.html: It sets how much one incoming number counts in a neuron
options.text: It sets how much one incoming number counts in a neuron
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A large weight makes an incoming number count for a lot, a weight near zero makes it nearly ignored, and a negative weight makes it count against.

forms.stemHtml: Two networks share one design. One was trained to identify animals in photographs and the other to tell indoor scenes from outdoor ones. Which statements about them are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: They have different numbers of layers and neurons
options.text: They have different numbers of layers and neurons
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

options.html: They differ in their parameter values
options.text: They differ in their parameter values
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The same design with different parameter settings does a different job.

options.html: They each contain the photographs they were trained on
options.text: They each contain the photographs they were trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on parameters.

options.html: They both began with randomly set parameters
options.text: They both began with randomly set parameters
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Every network starts with random parameter values, and training tunes them for the job.

forms.stemHtml: A model reaches a very low loss on its training examples. What does that result establish?

options.html: Its predictions are close on the examples that were scored
options.text: Its predictions are close on the examples that were scored
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A low loss is a statement about the examples that were scored. It says nothing about cases those examples didn't include.

options.html: Its predictions will be accurate on any input it is given
options.text: Its predictions will be accurate on any input it is given
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: Its parameters have each been checked by an engineer
options.text: Its parameters have each been checked by an engineer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

options.html: Its training data was free of gaps, skews, and wrong labels
options.text: Its training data was free of gaps, skews, and wrong labels
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on prediction error and loss.

forms.stemHtml: In one training step, a network makes predictions on some examples and its loss is computed. What does gradient descent then do with the network's parameters?

options.html: It replaces each parameter with a fresh random value
options.text: It replaces each parameter with a fresh random value
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: It removes the parameters that contributed to the error
options.text: It removes the parameters that contributed to the error
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: It tests every possible setting and keeps the lowest
options.text: It tests every possible setting and keeps the lowest
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on gradient descent and backpropagation.

options.html: It nudges each parameter slightly to lower the loss
options.text: It nudges each parameter slightly to lower the loss
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Gradient descent works out which way to nudge each parameter to lower the loss, then nudges each one slightly. Training repeats this step many times.

forms.stemHtml: A product name is invented after a model's vocabulary was settled, so the name isn't on the list. How can the model still take in a message that contains it?

options.html: The name is added to the vocabulary when first typed
options.text: The name is added to the vocabulary when first typed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: The name is built from pieces already on the list
options.text: The name is built from pieces already on the list
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The vocabulary is fixed, so an unfamiliar word is split into several subword tokens that the vocabulary already contains.

options.html: The name is matched to a known word by its spelling
options.text: The name is matched to a known word by its spelling
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

options.html: The name is looked up in a separate list of names
options.text: The name is looked up in a separate list of names
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on tokens and tokenization.

forms.stemHtml: In some sets of word embeddings, starting at "doctor" and taking the step from "man" to "woman" arrives at "nurse." Which statements about this are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: An engineer chose to link those two words
options.text: An engineer chose to link those two words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

options.html: The association came from patterns in the text
options.text: The association came from patterns in the text
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Embeddings record how words are used in the training text, and the association was in that text.

options.html: The result shows the embeddings failed to train
options.text: The result shows the embeddings failed to train
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on embeddings.

options.html: Embeddings can carry biases found in language
options.text: Embeddings can carry biases found in language
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Positions reflect how words are used in text, including its biases.

forms.stemHtml: A language model is partway through producing a long reply. What does it work from as it produces the next token?

options.html: The text so far, including its own tokens
options.text: The text so far, including its own tokens
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model has no finished reply in hand while it writes. It produces one token at a time, each predicted from the text so far.

options.html: A finished draft of the reply, released in parts
options.text: A finished draft of the reply, released in parts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: A stored answer that it is copying out in order
options.text: A stored answer that it is copying out in order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

options.html: An outline of the reply, drawn up before it began
options.text: An outline of the reply, drawn up before it began
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on next-token prediction.

title: Machine Learning and Language Models
